I checked the draft against the brand policy and found nothing that needs changing.

- **"We started Pebblebrook in Bristol in 2019"** matches the allowlist (founded in Bristol in 2019).
- **"Our tea bags are plastic-free and home compostable"** is an allowlisted claim, stated as written with no added qualifiers or upgrades.
- **"because we couldn't find tea bags without plastic in them"** is a founder-story motivation, not a statistic, superlative or guarantee. It doesn't claim that no plastic-free tea bags existed anywhere.
- **"here's how we checked"** is a lead-in to the rest of the post. This is only the intro, so I can't see what follows. Whatever the body says about the checking should stick to what the brand can support, such as the plastic-free and home compostable claims. It should not invent test results, percentages, timeframes, or third-party certifications beyond the Soil Association organic certification.
- There is no fake urgency, no testimonial, no health claim and no filler phrasing.
